summary: Re-tested the 3 CRITICAL bug fixes from iteration_2 + regressions. All 32 backend tests pass. The tz_aware fix in db.py resolves all three datetime-compare 500s: (1) POST /api/auth/refresh rotates correctly + reuse returns 401; (2) forgot→reset→login-with-new works, reused token returns 400; (3) brute-force lockout returns 429, never 500. Regression tests (RBAC 403 for viewer, editor create-record allowed, X-Org-Id override, tenant isolation, audit logs, /dev/seed-demo idempotency, slugify field-key regression, org create/switch, last-owner demotion blocked, register/login/me/logout) all pass.
critical_code_review_comments: Lockout key `IP:email` is fragile behind a load-balancing ingress: in this k8s preview env, ingress round-robins between ~2 upstream client IPs, effectively doubling the number of attempts needed to trigger lockout via public HTTP. Consider (a) trusting X-Forwarded-For / using request.headers.get('x-real-ip') for the identifier, or (b) an email-only fallback counter in addition to per-IP. Not a blocker; but the current implementation can be bypassed by any attacker that can force different source IPs (e.g., via multiple proxies).

rca of the issue: iteration_2's three 500s (refresh, reset-password, lockout on 6th attempt) had a single root cause: Motor was returning naive datetimes from BSON, which were then compared against tz-aware _now_dt() → TypeError → 500. Fix in /app/backend/db.py: AsyncIOMotorClient(MONGO_URL, tz_aware=True, tzinfo=timezone.utc). Verified via HTTP: no 500 status observed on any of the three affected code paths, and all functional assertions (rotation, single-use reset token, 429 lockout) succeed.
